text.p: British electronics component distributor Abacus Polar Plc said on Monday that cost efficiencies have helped it to outperform market expectations in its current financial year.
"I am pleased to report that the company has performed ahead of these expectations in the first quarter," Abacus' chairman Harry Westropp told shareholders at the company's annual general meeting.

Westropp was referring to his statement in the report and accounts in which he had forecast the firm's earnings per share in the first half of the current year would be "broadly similar" to that of the second half of 1996.
Abacus' EPS for its 12 months to September, 1996 stood at 13.5 pence.
The improvement, he said, was due mainly to cost savings made from the Abacus Polar merger although market conditions remained weak.
"We are confident of maintaining this improved performance to the interim stage," Westropp said.
Abacus' share price rose 8 1/2 pence to 212 1/2 at 1040 GMT.
